intro: Searching for health insurance near me usually means you want private medical cover and would rather speak to someone local who can explain the options face to face. You may be looking for cover for yourself or your family, or comparing it with what your employer offers. A local insurance broker can talk you through how private medical insurance works and what it might cost for your circumstances.
need_heading: What people searching for health insurance near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who search this way want straightforward, local help to understand private medical insurance and find cover that fits their health and budget.
needs: You want to know whether private medical insurance would let you see a consultant sooner for a planned operation or treatment.
You have a pre-existing condition and need to understand how insurers treat it and whether it can be covered.
You are comparing underwriting options and want to know the difference between full medical underwriting and moratorium underwriting.
You want to check which hospitals and specialists are included before you choose a policy.
You would like to understand how excesses work and how they affect what you pay for cover.
context_heading: Understanding pre-existing conditions and policy details
context: Private medical insurance pays for eligible private treatment for acute conditions, with options for outpatient cover and excesses. Pre-existing conditions are usually excluded, so it is important to be honest about your medical history when you apply. The way an insurer assesses your health can vary depending on the type of underwriting used.

Before you commit, check the hospital lists that come with each policy, as these can differ. A local insurance broker can explain the key features and exclusions and help you compare what is available in your area.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you are looking for private medical insurance and would like to speak to a local insurance broker.
Say who the cover is for, such as yourself, your family, or both.
Describe any pre-existing medical conditions or treatments you have had, as these will affect what is available.
Explain whether you have had private medical insurance before and whether you want to continue any cover.
Let us know if you have a preference for certain hospitals or consultants near you.
Tell us whether you are interested in outpatient cover and whether you have a budget in mind for the monthly cost.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the insurance broker
questions: How do you assess my pre-existing conditions, and will they be excluded or covered at a higher premium?
What is the difference between full medical underwriting and moratorium underwriting, and which suits me?
Which hospitals and specialists are included in the policies you are recommending?
How does the excess work, and what would I pay if I make a claim?
Are there any waiting periods before I can claim for certain treatments?
How are you paid for arranging my policy, and will you explain all the fees upfront?

faqs.q: Will private medical insurance cover my existing condition?
faqs.a: Pre-existing conditions are usually excluded from private medical insurance, but some insurers may offer cover with a higher premium or after a waiting period. It is important to disclose your full medical history so the broker can explain what is possible.

faqs.q: What is the difference between full medical underwriting and moratorium underwriting?
faqs.a: With full medical underwriting, you complete a medical questionnaire and the insurer decides upfront what will and will not be covered. With moratorium underwriting, you do not need to complete a full questionnaire, but conditions you have had in recent years may not be covered until a set period has passed.

faqs.q: Can I choose which hospital I go to?
faqs.a: Most policies have a list of hospitals you can use, and this can vary between insurers. You should check the hospital lists before you buy to make sure your preferred local hospitals are included.

faqs.q: How do insurance brokers get paid?
faqs.a: Brokers must tell you how they are paid, which is usually through a commission from the insurer or a fee you pay directly. You should ask for this to be explained clearly before you proceed.
